items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Well of all people, like the greatest, Ella Fitzgerald, was absolutely scared to death every night she had to go on the stage.

ctx.x: And I’ll tell you another thing too I mean, and I’ll question if he feels the same way, as long as I’ve been playing and in all the places that I have played, I mean all the big places, like he said at the White House and things like that and things for kings and queens. And I got a job in my hometown now because I live in Florida now you know. And I get the queasy stomach, I get nervous before I go to the job. I still get that feeling. But I want to keep that you know, I want to keep that feeling. Because…
Well of all people, like the greatest, Ella Fitzgerald, was absolutely scared to death every night she had to go on the stage. Scared to death. And she was the best.
That speaks of a certain humility. And talk to us about that. About the spirituality and staying humble before the music.
